ActivityAccepted.description:
How many were new. A repeat within the dedup window is accepted and not
recorded, which is a success rather than an error.
ActivityAccepted.title: ActivityAccepted

ActivityBatch.description:
A batch, because the browser sends these as it goes and a tab closing
should not lose the last few.
ActivityBatch.title: ActivityBatch

ActivityIn.description:
One thing the browser saw somebody do.

`ref_id` is a string because the six kinds live in three slices and one is
not a row at all; resolving a ref into a screen is the frontend's job.
ActivityIn.title: ActivityIn

AttemptBriefRead.description:
The reading-time screen, keyed on the attempt rather than the station.

On the attempt because that is what the entitlement check has already been
made against: `LibraryStationRead` deliberately carries no content, since
the library is browsable by everyone and the brief is part of the exam.
Once somebody has started a station, the brief is theirs to read.
AttemptBriefRead.title: AttemptBriefRead

AttemptHistoryItem.description:
One row of "what have I sat", with its station named.

`has_result` rather than a status the client has to interpret: "is there
feedback to open" is the only question every screen listing these asks.
AttemptHistoryItem.title: AttemptHistoryItem

AttemptReviewRead.description: The management step: what the candidate should have covered.
AttemptReviewRead.title: AttemptReviewRead

AudienceIn.description:
How a client says who something is for.

Lives in core beside the rule, like `Page` and `CursorParams`: three slices
take the same three fields, and three copies would drift.
AudienceIn.title: AudienceIn

AudienceOut.description: Who something is for, as a reader sees it.
AudienceOut.title: AudienceOut

BulkCreateTrainees.description:
A spreadsheet's worth of trainees in one request.

The browser parses the file; the API takes rows. Capped so one request
cannot invite a whole university at once by accident.
BulkCreateTrainees.title: BulkCreateTrainees

BulkTraineesResult.description: Who was added and who was not, so a partial upload is not a mystery.
BulkTraineesResult.title: BulkTraineesResult

CandidateScenarioRead.description:
Candidate-facing keys that sit flat on the document rather than in a block.

Ortho's stations are shaped this way: an interview or a trauma list rather
than a consultation, so the brief is a scenario and a set of images.
CandidateScenarioRead.title: CandidateScenarioRead

Capabilities.description:
What the caller may do, decided here rather than in the browser.

The B2B frontend keeps a table mirroring the backend policy and uses it to
decide whether to issue a request at all. Two copies of an authorisation
rule is one too many; this is the served answer.
Capabilities.title: Capabilities

CheckoutStarted.description: Where to send the customer. Nothing is granted until the webhook.
CheckoutStarted.title: CheckoutStarted

CircuitConsole.description: One request for the screen a supervisor runs an examination from.
CircuitConsole.title: CircuitConsole

CloudCapacityRead.description:
How full LiveKit Cloud is, for the people watching it.

`active` is None when Redis cannot be asked, which is also what routes a
new session to our own workers — so None here is the thing to look at.
CloudCapacityRead.title: CloudCapacityRead

CloudSlotPost.description:
What the worker posts. `room_name` is fixed by `slot_payload_key` in its
own configuration, so the field name is part of the contract.
CloudSlotPost.title: CloudSlotPost

CohortCandidate.description: One candidate's standing in a sitting.
CohortCandidate.title: CohortCandidate

CohortSummary.description:
How a sitting's candidates compare, ranked.

Exam sittings only. A training circuit is people practising, and ranking
them against each other would turn practice into an assessment nobody
agreed to sit.
CohortSummary.title: CohortSummary

ConsoleStation.description: Null fields mean the version is not readable by this org, not that it is untitled.
ConsoleStation.title: ConsoleStation

CreateAttempt.description:
What a client may ask for directly.

Deliberately narrower than `attempts.create_attempt`. The other kinds are
*about* something a different slice owns — a slot, a set entry, a peer
pairing, an earlier attempt — and `attempts` sits below all of them in the
layer order, so it cannot check that the caller owns the thing they named.

This route used to take every one of those ids straight from the body and
store them unverified, which let anyone attach their attempt to another
organisation's exam slot or another person's set entry. Each of those
kinds has its own route, on the slice that can do the checking:
`POST /me/station-sets/{set_id}/entries/{entry_id}/attempts` for a set
station and its debrief, and the circuit itself for an exam slot (ADR
0018). `room_name` is likewise not the client's to choose — `voice`
derives it from the attempt.
CreateAttempt.title: CreateAttempt

CreateProgramme.description:
The exam this programme groups sittings under.

By code, resolved in the institution's own scope first: a school that has
written its own `plab` gets that one, not the platform's.
CreateProgramme.title: CreateProgramme

CreditSignup.description:
Ties the signed-in account to the visit that brought them.

Sent after registering, with the key the arrival was logged under. The
browser holds it; the backend never sees a partner cookie.
CreditSignup.title: CreditSignup

Dashboard.description:
Replaces seven calls on the SCA dashboard alone.

The legacy screen fans out to four RAG endpoints, a weekly trend and two
marketplace lists, then joins them in the browser.
Dashboard.title: Dashboard

DirectoryUser.description:
One row of the directory: the seven columns the retiring console had,
each answered by the slice that owns the fact.
DirectoryUser.title: DirectoryUser

DoctorInformationRead.description: The candidate's brief: what the doctor has in front of them.
DoctorInformationRead.title: DoctorInformationRead

DomainScore.description: One bar of the radar: a rubric domain, averaged across the attempts.
DomainScore.title: DomainScore

ExamDirectorySummary.description: How many accounts an exam has, split the way the old filter did.
ExamDirectorySummary.title: ExamDirectorySummary

ExtendEntitlement.description: Move the end date. `None` makes the grant open-ended.
ExtendEntitlement.title: ExtendEntitlement

ortho_station_type.description: When exam_code is ortho: clinical, communication, prioritisation, or portfolio.
ortho_station_type.title: Ortho Station Type

GrantEntitlement.description:
An institution granting one of its people access to an exam it runs.

By email, as everything an administrator does is. `ends_at` left empty is
open-ended; an institution usually sets it to the end of the academic year.
GrantEntitlement.title: GrantEntitlement

JobRead.description: One queued job as procrastinate holds it.
JobRead.title: JobRead

JobsPage.description: Newest first, keyed on the job id; pass `next_before_id` back to continue.
JobsPage.title: JobsPage

LegacyExchangeRequest.description:
Trade a token one of the legacy backends issued for a platform pair.

`provider` is a closed set rather than a string because it selects the
secret the token is verified against; an open one would let the caller
choose its own key.
LegacyExchangeRequest.title: LegacyExchangeRequest

LibraryStationRead.description:
A platform library station as it appears in a browse list.

Deliberately without `content`. The library is browsable by every signed-in
user, and the content is the patient brief, the examiner's context and the
marking guidance — reading it before sitting the station is reading the
answers. `version_id` is what a practice set or a circuit binds, so a
caller never needs the body to use one.
LibraryStationRead.title: LibraryStationRead

LiveBoard.description:
Everything running in one organisation, in one request.

`as_of` is the server time the numbers were computed against, so a client
can count down from the deadlines rather than waiting to be told again.
LiveBoard.title: LiveBoard

LiveCircuit.description: One examination in progress, as a row on the board.
LiveCircuit.title: LiveCircuit

LiveStation.description: The station a candidate is on now. Null when the circuit is on a break.
LiveStation.title: LiveStation

LogoutRequest.description:
The session to end.

Optional: without it every session ends, which is what "sign me out
everywhere" means. With it only the presented chain goes, so signing out on
a phone leaves the laptop signed in.
LogoutRequest.title: LogoutRequest

ManagementPlanRead.description: The model answer, readable once the consultation is over.
ManagementPlanRead.title: ManagementPlanRead

MessageAccepted.description: Deliberately thin: an id, so support can be quoted one, and nothing else.
MessageAccepted.title: MessageAccepted

MySittings.description:
The trainee portal's whole screen, in one request.

It polls two lists every five seconds and joins them in the browser to
answer one question: is it my turn yet?
MySittings.title: MySittings

MySlot.description: A station this person is rostered onto, from their side of it.
MySlot.title: MySlot

OrgAtRisk.description: An organisation the console should look at before it looks at anything else.
OrgAtRisk.title: OrgAtRisk

OrgCounts.description: What the setup checklist counts. Four legacy calls existed to produce these.
OrgCounts.title: OrgCounts

OrgSetup.description:
Whether the organisation can actually hold a sitting yet.

Each flag is a step the browser was deriving from a list it fetched only to
take the length of.
OrgSetup.title: OrgSetup

Override.description:
What every override may carry: why it was done.

Optional, and free text, because the reasons are the ones nobody predicted
— that is what an override is for. It is written to the record beside the
action, so "the clock was extended" is answerable with "because the fire
alarm went".
Override.title: Override

PatientIdentityRead.description: Who the candidate is about to speak to, for the consultation header.
PatientIdentityRead.title: PatientIdentityRead

PatientReviewRead.description:
The patient's side, as a candidate may read it afterwards.

Not a passthrough: `persona`, `opening_sentence`, `expanded_history` and
the hidden question list are how the patient is played, and they stay on
the server. What is here is what the old management screen showed — the
biodata line and the ideas, concerns and expectations the candidate was
supposed to draw out.
PatientReviewRead.title: PatientReviewRead

Performance.description:
The charts on the consumer exam dashboard, in one call.

The legacy screen asks four RAG endpoints and a weekly trend for this and
joins them in the browser. `exam_code` is null only when the caller named
no exam and has never attempted one — there is no exam to report on, and
an empty string would be a code.
Performance.title: Performance

PerformanceSummary.description:
How the marked attempts divide, as rates rather than counts.

Rates because the chart draws bands, and because a candidate with four
attempts and one with forty should read the same way.
PerformanceSummary.title: PerformanceSummary

PlatformAttemptRead.description:
An attempt, with the state a support question turns on.

`scoring_job` is the newest marking job for it, or None when nothing was
ever queued — which with a complete transcript is itself the diagnosis.
PlatformAttemptRead.title: PlatformAttemptRead

PlatformAuditRead.description:
An audit row as the console reads it across every organisation.

`org_id` is None for the platform's own acts; `meta` is whatever the
action recorded beyond its summary, such as the old and new value.
PlatformAuditRead.title: PlatformAuditRead

PlatformEntitlementRead.description: A grant as the platform console reads it: where it came from, who made it.
PlatformEntitlementRead.title: PlatformEntitlementRead

PlatformGrantEntitlement.description:
A platform admin granting access outright — a refund made good, a
sponsor's seat, a support gesture. `note` is why, and goes in the audit row.
PlatformGrantEntitlement.title: PlatformGrantEntitlement

PlatformHealth.description: The liveness report plus what only the console needs: the queue and the worker.
PlatformHealth.title: PlatformHealth

PlatformPaymentRead.description: A payment as the console reads it: raw amounts, both references, what it bought.
PlatformPaymentRead.title: PlatformPaymentRead

PlatformUserDetail.description: Support view: memberships and account flags the list row omits.
PlatformUserDetail.title: PlatformUserDetail

PrioritisationPatientRead.description: One patient on an Ortho prioritisation list.
PrioritisationPatientRead.title: PrioritisationPatientRead

QueueStatus.description:
Where someone stands, and what to do next.

`position` is why this is one call: b2c polls a status endpoint every three
seconds, and it should be able to answer "am I matched yet?" in one round
trip.
QueueStatus.title: QueueStatus

RebuildCircuit.description:
A circuit's new shape. Everything omitted is left as it is.

The trainees and the stations are sent whole rather than as a patch: the
slots are rebuilt from them, and a partial edit would leave the API
guessing which pairing the supervisor meant.
RebuildCircuit.title: RebuildCircuit

ReceiptRead.description:
A payment receipt, rendered.

Every field is a string already formatted for display: a receipt is read by
people rather than parsed by clients, and rendering money and dates in the
browser is how two surfaces come to show the same payment differently.
ReceiptRead.title: ReceiptRead

RecordArrival.description: Public: a visitor landing from a partner link, before any account exists.
RecordArrival.title: RecordArrival

RecordManualPayment.description:
A payment that did not come through Stripe — a bank transfer, a sponsor,
a comped seat — recorded so it grants access, mints a receipt and counts
like any other. Without a reference one is minted as `manual:<id>`.
RecordManualPayment.title: RecordManualPayment

RefundRequest.description:
Record-only: the money is returned in the Stripe dashboard. This revokes
what the payment bought and says so in the audit log; the payment row stays.
RefundRequest.title: RefundRequest

ReindexReport.description: What a re-index did, so an admin can tell "ran" from "found nothing".
ReindexReport.title: ReindexReport

RenewContract.description:
New dates, and whether a suspension should lift with them.

One call rather than a `PATCH` and a `restore`: a renewal that sets the
date and forgets to restore leaves a paying customer locked out.
RenewContract.title: RenewContract

RescoreRequest.description:
Re-queue the marking. Left empty, under the policy the attempt was
frozen with; named, under another one, whose result sits beside the old.
RescoreRequest.title: RescoreRequest

ResolveRosterRequest.description: Who a circuit would name, before it is built.
ResolveRosterRequest.title: ResolveRosterRequest

ResolvedRoster.description:
Who a circuit would actually contain, and what is missing.

Returned before a circuit is built so a supervisor sees an empty linked
group now rather than when the examination starts.
ResolvedRoster.title: ResolvedRoster

ResultAcknowledgement.description: A candidate's confirmation that they have read their result.
ResultAcknowledgement.title: ResultAcknowledgement

SaveGpLeadReview.description:
`revision` is what the client last read.

Required, so a client that does not send it cannot overwrite blindly.
SaveGpLeadReview.title: SaveGpLeadReview

ScoringJobRead.description: One marking job as the queue holds it.
ScoringJobRead.title: ScoringJobRead

SetPlatformAdmin.description: Grant or revoke, spelled out rather than implied by which route was called.
SetPlatformAdmin.title: SetPlatformAdmin

SiteStatistics.description:
The counters the landing page's numbers band shows.

Marketing figures, not analytics: they are rounded down to a readable
number and they are cached, because the busiest page on the site should not
cost five aggregate queries per view.
SiteStatistics.title: SiteStatistics

SlotRagSummary.description:
What several reviewers of one slot agreed, or did not.

The worst rating wins per domain, which is b2b's tie-break and worth
keeping: when two reviewers disagree about a candidate, the lower rating is
the one that should prompt a conversation. Computed here rather than in the
browser so a supervisor's screen, a released result and an export cannot
each arrive at a different answer.
SlotRagSummary.title: SlotRagSummary

SsoConfigRead.description: The whole arrangement, for whoever administers it.
SsoConfigRead.title: SsoConfigRead

SsoSignIn.description:
What a sign-in page may know before anybody has proved anything.

Deliberately thin. This is served without a token, to anyone who asks, so
it carries what a button needs and nothing about the organisation beyond
the name it already puts on its own front page. No issuer, no bindings, no
counts: those are configuration, and configuration is for administrators.
SsoSignIn.title: SsoSignIn

StartCheckout.description: Which plan to buy. A code, never a price: the plan row owns the price.
StartCheckout.title: StartCheckout

StartedAttempt.description:
What starting a set entry returns.

Deliberately this slice's own shape rather than `attempts`' response model.
They would look alike today and diverge the moment either contract moves,
and a client of one should not break because the other added a field.
StartedAttempt.title: StartedAttempt

StationProgressChange.description: What one of the two actions did, in numbers the toast can print.
StationProgressChange.title: StationProgressChange

StationProgressRead.description:
One station this person has sat, or holds in a practice set.

`attempts` counts the attempts that exist; `entry_attempts` is the sum of
the counters on their set entries, which is what the per-station limit is
enforced on and what "reset attempts" zeroes. The two agree until somebody
resets, and showing both is how the console explains the difference.
StationProgressRead.title: StationProgressRead

StationTeachingRead.description: Ortho's flat teaching keys: the debrief material for a non-consultation station.
StationTeachingRead.title: StationTeachingRead

StreamTicket.description:
A short-lived credential for one `EventSource` connection.

`EventSource` cannot send an `Authorization` header; see `core.streams` for
why this exists rather than a cookie or a token in the query string.
StreamTicket.title: StreamTicket

StripeEventRead.description:
One webhook delivery from the ledger, with the fields support reads
out of the payload rather than the whole document.
StripeEventRead.title: StripeEventRead

SupervisorCircuitRow.description: One circuit this person is named on, with the sitting it belongs to.
SupervisorCircuitRow.title: SupervisorCircuitRow

SwitchWorkspace.description:
Which workspace to re-issue the token against.

`None` means the person's own practice. That is a real destination, not an
absence: somebody who belongs to an institution still has their own
entitlements and their own attempts, and without this there is no way back
to them once an organisation is active.
SwitchWorkspace.title: SwitchWorkspace

ToolCall.description:
What the worker posts for one tool call.

`call_id` is the worker's own and is echoed nowhere; it is here because the
worker sends it and a rejected extra field would fail the call.
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolResult.description:
What the model reads, and what the browser is shown.

`result` is spoken, so it is prose rather than data. `display` is passed to
the frontend unchanged on the data channel; the backend never composes a
route, because which screen a thing lives on is the frontend's business.
ToolResult.title: ToolResult

TrackingReference.description: What a partner puts in one link, and where that link points.
TrackingReference.title: TrackingReference

TraineeResultRead.description:
What a candidate sees.

Deliberately narrower than the internal record: moderation notes and the
evidence snapshot are ours, not theirs. b2b's own schema doc says not to
reproduce disclosure policy in frontend transforms — so it is applied here.
TraineeResultRead.title: TraineeResultRead

TrendPoint.description: One attempt, in the order it was sat.
TrendPoint.title: TrendPoint

TutorMemoryRead.description:
Everything the tutor holds about you, in the order it would speak it.

Exists so "what do you know about me" is answerable without reading a
prompt: a memory nobody can inspect is one nobody can correct.
TutorMemoryRead.title: TutorMemoryRead

UpdateBrief.description: The one field a published version will accept a change to.
UpdateBrief.title: UpdateBrief

UpdateExam.description: Everything but the code, which existing plans and ref ids depend on.
UpdateExam.title: UpdateExam

UpdateMe.description: What a person may change about themselves. Absent means "leave it".
UpdateMe.title: UpdateMe

UpdateOrganization.description:
What a platform administrator may change about an organisation.

Not the slug: every foreign key points at `id` and the slug is the URL, so
renaming one is a redirect problem rather than a field edit.
UpdateOrganization.title: UpdateOrganization

UserSummary.description: An account as the console lists it. No password state, no memberships.
UserSummary.title: UserSummary

VoiceGrant.description:
What the browser needs to join, and nothing more.

No agent name and no backend label: those are dispatch details the client
has no use for, and b2c currently hands the browser a metadata blob it
simply passes back.
VoiceGrant.title: VoiceGrant

WorkerBootstrap.description:
`{attempt, scenario}` — the only thing a worker is told.

Both halves are passed through as the engine's own documents rather than
re-modelled here: re-describing them would create a second definition of a
contract the engine already owns, free to drift.
WorkerBootstrap.title: WorkerBootstrap

WorkerSessionPayload.description:
`{"session": {...}}` — the shape `livekit_assistant_worker` validates.

Its paths are hardcoded in the worker rather than configured per backend, so
this API must mount them exactly. Noted in the README.
WorkerSessionPayload.title: WorkerSessionPayload

app__features__assistant__schemas__RoomG.description:
What the browser needs to join this session's room, and nothing more.

The same three fields `voice` returns for a circuit's room. Restated here
rather than imported because a router may name only its own slice's
schemas, and the response shape is this route's contract either way.
app__features__assistant__schemas__RoomG.title: RoomGrant

app__features__identity__schemas__Accept.description: Returned where the answer must not depend on whether a record exists.
app__features__identity__schemas__Accept.title: Accepted

app__features__media__schemas__MediaRead.description:
One piece of study material.

`content` is the body — the slide deck, the summary, the article — and it
is the paid half. It is `None` for a reader who does not hold the exam it
belongs to, and `locked` says which of the two happened, so the client can
show the upgrade prompt the retiring app showed rather than an empty page.

Everything else is deliberately public: the landing page's article rail and
a shared link both need a title and a summary without a token.
app__features__media__schemas__MediaRead.title: MediaRead

app__features__media_production__schemas.description: Same fields as media's item read, owned here so this slice's contract stands alone.
app__features__media_production__schemas.title: MediaRead

app__features__peer_practice__schemas__R.description:
What a browser needs to join a peer session's room.

This slice's own shape rather than `voice`'s or `sittings`', for the
reason those two do not share one either: a wire contract belongs to the
routes that serve it.
app__features__peer_practice__schemas__R.title: RoomGrant

app__features__sittings__schemas__RoomGr.description:
What a browser needs to join a circuit's room, and nothing more.

A candidate taking their place before their station starts, or an examiner
stepping in to watch. Neither names a recording: the candidate has none yet
and the examiner never will, which is what separates this from the token
issued against an attempt.

This slice's own shape rather than `voice`'s, even though the two agree
today: a wire contract belongs to the routes that serve it, and sharing one
is how two slices come to be unable to change it separately.
app__features__sittings__schemas__RoomGr.title: RoomGrant

post.description:
Rebuild the material index now, rather than waiting for tonight's run.

Synchronous on purpose, unlike most admin actions here. An author who has
just published a correction wants to know it is searchable, and a job id to
go and poll answers a different question. The whole library is thousands of
passages, which is a request that takes a while, not one that times out.
The browser's way into an assistant session's room.

The candidate walks away before finishing.

Otherwise the attempt stays `running` forever, holding the slot's one live
attempt and counting as in progress on every screen that reads it.

get.description:
What the candidate reads before the patient is called.

Keyed on the attempt, not the station: the library's own read carries no
content on purpose, because browsing is open to everybody and the brief is
part of the exam. Having started the station is what makes it readable.

A page rather than one result: re-scoring under a new policy adds beside
the old, so a candidate's history stays readable.

The model answer: the patient's ideas and concerns, and the plan.

Refused until the consultation is over — before that it is the answer to
the station being sat.

The attempt, pushed until it is marked.

Marking is a background job taking a minute or two of model time, so the
page has to learn it finished. This replaces b2c's feedback-status
stream, its poller and the second poller behind that.

200.description: An SSE stream: `connected`, then a `snapshot` frame whose `data` is a `AttemptRead` each time the state changes, and `ping` every 25 seconds.

post.description: Sign in here with the session the old backend already gave you.
Ends the presented session, or every session when none is named.

get.description:
Whether this visitor's organisation signs in somewhere else.

**Unauthenticated, and it has to be**: this is what a sign-in page asks
before anybody has signed in. The retiring client answered it from a
hostname allow-list compiled into the bundle, so adding a partner meant a
frontend deploy and the tenant slug, the button's wording and the
"no password form" rule were three things that could disagree with the
backend.

A 404 means "sign in here, with a password", which is the ordinary case and
what every host that is not a partner's gets.

parameters.description: The hostname the visitor arrived at, for a white-label site.
parameters.name: host

schema.description: The hostname the visitor arrived at, for a white-label site.
schema.title: Host

parameters.description: An address typed into the ordinary sign-in form.
parameters.name: email

schema.description: An address typed into the ordinary sign-in form.
schema.title: Email

post.description:
A sixty-second credential a browser can put in a stream's URL.

Minted with an ordinary bearer token, spent immediately on one
`text/event-stream` connection, and refused by every other route.

Begin paying for a plan.

The client names a plan code and never a price or an amount: b2c matched
the pence paid against a hardcoded table, so a price change broke
purchases after the card was charged.

get.description:
Public: the pricing page reads this rather than hardcoding amounts, which
is how b2c's client and server came to disagree about what a plan costs.

post.description:
Apply one delivery, at most once, and only if Stripe sent it.

The **raw body** is what the signature covers, so it is read and verified
before being parsed. Declaring a parsed body parameter instead would hand
FastAPI the bytes first and leave the signature checking something else.

delete.description:
Your own, anyone's if you are a platform admin, or anything addressed
inside an institution you administer.

b2c's delete routes carry no decorator at all, so anyone can remove anyone's.

post.description: Idempotent. b2c increments a counter, so a double tap counts twice.

get.description:
Everything this caller may see, or one room of it.

Without a filter the answer spans the public pool and every institution and
group the caller belongs to, which is what a single feed should be.

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page
parameters.name: cursor

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page
schema.title: Cursor

get.description:
The exams the platform offers. Small set, so no cursor is ever returned.

The consumer catalogue: platform exams only. An institution's own exams are
not here and never are — they are that institution's, not ours to publish.
See `/orgs/{org_slug}/exams` for those.

A platform admin sees the platform's drafts, because they are the person
writing them, and nobody else's.

post.description:
Credit this new account to whoever sent them, once.

Its own route rather than a step inside registering: `growth` sits above
`identity`, so registration cannot call it, and a partner who sent somebody
was credited with nothing at all until this existed. Null when there is
nothing to credit, which is the ordinary case.

Public: a visitor arriving from a partner link, before any account exists.

Unauthenticated by necessity — there is nobody to authenticate yet — which
is why the partner must be a known one and the visitor key is opaque.

get.description:
Checked against the partner in the path, so one partner's reporter
cannot read another's numbers.

The references this partner puts in its links, one per exam in the pilot.

Reporter-gated like the funnel: a reference is commercially meaningful, and
one partner has no business reading another's.

post.description: Platform admin only: partners do not appoint their own reporters.

get.description:
Availability and claimed slots this caller can see — the public pool plus
every institution and group they belong to. Matches the retiring marketplace
feed (open posts plus historic claimed sessions).

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page
parameters.name: cursor

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page
schema.title: Cursor

post.description:
Claimed once. The row is locked before it is examined, so the second of
two simultaneous claims is told the slot is gone rather than double-booked.

patch.description:
Change a person's own profile: their name, their exam date, their
reading-time arrangement.

Only what was sent is written — `model_fields_set` rather than the whole
body, so a screen that edits one field does not silently clear the others.

post.description:
What this person has been reading and practising.

A batch, and accepted rather than created: the browser sends these as it
goes, often as a tab is closing, and a repeat inside the dedup window is a
success that records nothing.

get.description:
Everything this person has sat, newest first.
